name: Alluzience

lead: Alluzience is a liquid form of abobotulinumtoxinA (the toxin in Dysport/Azzalure) from Ipsen and Galderma. It was the first ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin A approved in Europe for glabellar (frown) lines.
It relaxes the small muscles that crease the skin, smoothing lines. Its main difference from powder toxins is that no mixing is needed before injection.

paras: A clinician injects it into facial muscles; no reconstitution step is needed. An international consensus describes its use for frown lines and for other areas such as crow's feet, forehead lines, brow lift, masseter hypertrophy and platysmal bands.
As with botulinum toxins generally, risks include spread of toxin to nearby muscles causing temporary weakness or drooping; it is prescription-only and given by trained clinicians.

angle.text: Injected into frown-line muscles, it reduces creasing; consensus guidance also covers brow shaping, jaw (masseter) slimming and neck bands.

lead: Alluzience (abobotulinumtoxinA RTU, from Ipsen and Galderma) is the first ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin type A solution approved in Europe for glabellar lines.[1] Most botulinum toxins are powders that must be reconstituted before injection; the liquid form was developed to ease injection and prevent reconstitution errors.[2]

In a Phase IV randomized trial in women with prior toxin experience, ready-to-use abobotulinumtoxinA needed less preparation time than powder onabotulinumtoxinA (mean 0:33 versus 1:34 minutes), and investigators preferred it.[2] An international consensus statement from the Alluzience board lists aesthetic uses beyond glabellar lines, including crow's feet, forehead lines, lateral brow lift, bunny lines, perioral wrinkles, masseter hypertrophy and platysmal bands.[1]
The toxin family carries FDA boxed warnings about spread from the injection site, issued in 2009.[3]

paras: Approved indication is glabellar lines in Europe.[1] The consensus recommendations additionally describe off-label areas: crow's feet, horizontal forehead lines, lateral eyebrow lift, lower eyelid wrinkles, bunny lines, drooping nasal tip, perioral wrinkles, drooping mouth corners, masseter hypertrophy, hollow cheek lines, dimpled chin and platysmal bands.[1]

A multicenter, open-label Phase IV study randomized 150 experienced female patients 2:1 to 50 U ready-to-use abobotulinumtoxinA or 20 U powder onabotulinumtoxinA; the liquid took significantly less time to prepare, and investigators preferred it.[2] Subject satisfaction and aesthetic improvement were assessed for the liquid over 6 months.[2]
Potency of liquid and powder abobotulinumtoxinA was shown to be measurable with a cell-based assay in place of the mouse LD50 test, with equivalence demonstrated for the liquid formulation.[4]

In 2009 the FDA required boxed warnings on botulinum toxin products about spread from the injection site, and noted the products are not interchangeable.[3] General adverse effects include temporary weakness of unintended muscles, double vision, facial weakness and headache.[3]

timeline.event: FDA requires boxed warnings on botulinum toxins regarding distant spread.[3]
